Coordinator was empathetic about the phone-menu problem, waived the fee per policy, rebooked promptly and did a warm transfer
Nurse did a thorough symptom triage with clear safety-net instructions (urgent care if over 300 or symptoms)

decoys.text: Fasting glucose of 240 handled by the nurse without sending the patient to the ER
decoys.why_not: The nurse triaged properly (no vomiting, confusion, abdominal pain or breathing trouble), gave clear thresholds (over 300 or symptoms -> urgent care/ER same day), sent strips, and booked a nurse visit Monday. Correct escalation.
decoys.evidence: If you see anything over three hundred, or if you start vomiting, or get belly pain, or feel confused, or really short of breath, you go to urgent care or the ER that same day
paraphrases: A blood sugar of 240 was not treated as an emergency; the nurse only advised home monitoring.
Hyperglycemia (glucose 240) was dismissed instead of urgent evaluation.
Nurse should have sent the patient to urgent care for the high sugar reading.

decoys.why_not: She states policy: the fee is waived automatically for the first missed visit in 12 months.
decoys.evidence: it's your first missed visit in twelve months, so per our policy that's waived automatically
paraphrases: The agent removed the forty-dollar no-show fee without approval.
No-show fee was waived outside policy.
